title: Connection tool: find the leak round a ring that separates nothing (L), and cut across it at its narrowest strait (Enter)
user-messages:
> The grow tool and the connection tool’s additions

split into two tickets
description:
Two additions to the ring scene's connection tool: the L key finds the way round a ring that separates nothing (a leak), and Enter cuts a bisector across that path at its narrowest strait. Split out of the stroke-segmentation worktree (CRAW-105), where they were built without a ticket.

## What exists

Additions to `ConnectionTool` (the leak finder and the cut), and `BisectorTool.draftAcross` with `nearestWall` (the cut across a path's narrowest strait).

## What the review found

From ai-workspace `reports/craw-105-uncommitted-review-2026-11-12.md` (part 5):

- Hand-picked numbers with no ticket listing them: `STRAITS_TRIED = 12`, and the "middle half" window of the path that `draftAcross` searches.
- No tests.
- A field named `centroids` that does not hold centroids.
- The tool switches before it knows the cut succeeded.
- One wall search per path point.
- A new log line.

`BisectorTool.draftAlong` (a bisector along a drawn or grown line) is in the same file; which ticket it belongs to is an open question.
definition-of-done: 1. Every number the leak finder and the cut use is listed on this ticket for the user to decide. 2. Unit tests cover finding a leak and cutting across it on a shape with a known strait. 3. The tool switches only after the cut succeeds. 4. A launch.json entry and a screenshot under tmp/ show a leak closed on a scan.
testing-plan: 1. Unit test: on a shape where one ring separates nothing because of a single strait, L finds the path through that strait. 2. Unit test: Enter cuts a bisector across the strait and the ring then separates two regions. 3. Run both on the IMG_4113 crawfish abdomen, where touching side flaps make a ring separate nothing, and screenshot the result.
